title: Why Plane Toilets Still Need Ashtrays (Smoking Banned Since 2000) ✈️
description:
Why does a no-smoking plane toilet have an ashtray? Smoking on every US flight has been banned since 2000, yet the rules still demand an ashtray on or near every lavatory door.

Because the real danger isn't the smoker, it's where the cigarette ends up. Someone who breaks the rule may panic and hide it, and the nearest hiding spot is a bin full of paper towels. So the rule gives them one obvious, safe place to put it out first. The bin even has its own small automatic fire extinguisher, and a smoke detector watches the room.

Have you ever noticed the ashtray on a plane? Tell us below.

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: US Code of Federal Regulations, 14 CFR 25.853 and 25.854 (lavatory ashtrays, smoke detectors, waste-bin extinguishers); FAA Amendment 25-74 (1991); Marketplace (2024); CNN (2017).
Animation, music and sound: TrueWhys (original). 3D people: MPFB 2 (CC0 output). Fonts: Lilita One (Open Font License).
